Two things to assert on any response: its **status code** and its **body**.
`Status Should Be    200    ${resp}` checks the code. `${resp.json()}` parses
the JSON body, and you index into it like a dictionary: `${resp.json()}[slug]`.

## Task 1 — Assert a product's status and JSON fields

**Goal:** create `checks/json.robot` that GETs the `travel-mug` product, asserts
a `200`, and checks its `slug` and `price` fields.

Here is the same status-and-field check on a different product. Adapt it to
`travel-mug` and add the price.

<!-- example -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library     RequestsLibrary
Resource    ../resources/api.resource

*** Test Cases ***
Backpack Has Expected Fields
    ${resp}=    GET    ${API_URL}/api/products/trail-backpack
    Status Should Be    200    ${resp}
    Should Be Equal    ${resp.json()}[slug]    trail-backpack
```
<!-- /example -->

**Check:** the response is 200 and its fields match.

<!-- hint -->
GET `${API_URL}/api/products/travel-mug`, check `Status Should Be    200`, and
assert `Should Be Equal    ${resp.json()}[slug]    travel-mug`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- hint -->
Assert the price too. It is a number, so use
`Should Be Equal As Numbers    ${resp.json()}[price]    19.90`.
<!-- /hint -->
<!-- solution -->
```robotframework
*** Settings ***
Library     RequestsLibrary
Resource    ../resources/api.resource

*** Test Cases ***
Product Has Expected Fields
    ${resp}=    GET    ${API_URL}/api/products/travel-mug
    Status Should Be    200    ${resp}
    Should Be Equal    ${resp.json()}[slug]    travel-mug
    Should Be Equal As Numbers    ${resp.json()}[price]    19.90
```
<!-- /solution -->

## Task 2 — Run it green

Run:

```bash
uv run robot checks
```

**Check:** the test `Product Has Expected Fields` passes.
